title: PDE and Domain Bridge

distributional_hdiv_bridge: complex L2 graph coordinates embedded canonically into tempered distributions
continuous distributional-divergence graph defect with a closed kernel relation encoding div(q) = g
smooth complex H(div) graph core and its topological closure map into the true distributional graph relation
explicit real-v3.28-to-complex graph map with Schwartz derivative/divergence compatibility
every field in the actual v3.28 real H(div) graph closure has a genuine distributional InHDiv complex image
bounded_box_bridge: box L2 spaces use volume.restrict (Set.Icc a b)
box H1 and H(div) smooth graph maps, graph cores, topological closures, and dense smooth cores
continuous bounded-box Green volume pairing and functional normal trace on the closed graph spaces
restricted-L2 inner products on Schwartz fields are identified with classical box integrals
the smooth closure trace is reduced to the classical Green volume integral and then to signed face flux under the hypotheses of the machine-checked smooth box Green theorem
dense-core uniqueness theorem characterizes any continuous extension agreeing with the box trace on the common dense smooth cores

ranked_next_proofs.goal: Discharge the classical product-derivative hypotheses automatically for arbitrary Schwartz scalar/vector core fields, so the smooth trace-to-face-flux theorem no longer requires externally supplied F', Hd, Hi, or hprod witnesses.
Prove a genuine graph-norm mollification/density theorem yielding the reverse inclusion from arbitrary distributional H(div) graph data to the smooth graph closure in a precisely stated domain scope.

Use the bounded-box classical trace bridge to package the PDE-domain weak Green and zero-boundary orthogonality results directly for the box graph model and feed them into the continuum Prager-Synge endpoint.

nonclaims: The latest bounded-box classical-agreement additions are not marked FORMAL_CI_PASS until an exact-head pinned GitHub Actions run actually executes and succeeds.
The real v3.28 graph closure maps into the complex distributional H(div) relation, but reverse inclusion is not yet proved.
No reverse inclusion from arbitrary distributional H(div) data to the smooth graph closure is claimed without a graph-norm density/mollification theorem.
No zero-extension theorem is assumed to commute with divergence across a box boundary.
The smooth trace agreement theorem currently retains the explicit smooth Green/product-derivative hypotheses instead of claiming they have all been discharged automatically for every Schwartz pair.
